original_question: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system with length function ell and reflection set T = {wsw^-1 : s in S, w in W}. It is known that sum_{u in W} x^{ell(u)} is a rational generating function. Determine whether sum_{t in T} x^{ell(t)} must also be a rational generating function.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.1 (the Stembridge problem on the rationality of the reflection-length generating function).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it uses the correct setting of a Coxeter system (W,S), the Coxeter length function ℓ, the correct definition of the reflection set T={wsw^-1 : s∈S, w∈W}, recalls the standard rationality of the ordinary Poincaré series Σ_{u∈W} x^{ℓ(u)}, and asks exactly whether the reflection series Σ_{t∈T} x^{ℓ(t)} is rational.
missing_details: The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether this holds for every Coxeter system (W,S), not just for a particular one.
The paper’s definition of a Coxeter system includes that S is finite; this is implicit in your draft.
It is worth stating that W is not assumed finite; the problem is posed for arbitrary Coxeter systems.
The variable x should be identified as an indeterminate.

To make the question fully stand-alone, 'is a rational generating function' should be read in the standard sense that the formal power series Σ_{t∈T} x^{ℓ(t)} is represented by a rational function in x.
The nearby context in the paper notes that no partial results seem to be known; this is not part of the statement itself, but it is part of the paper-faithful framing.
refined_question: For every Coxeter system (W,S), where S is finite, let ℓ:W→N be the Coxeter length function and let T={wsw^{-1}: s∈S, w∈W} be the set of reflections. It is known that the ordinary Poincaré series Σ_{u∈W} x^{ℓ(u)} is a rational function of the indeterminate x. Must the reflection-length series Σ_{t∈T} x^{ℓ(t)} also be a rational function in x?
justification: The draft is already tightly aligned with the paper’s exact target: Brenti states this as Problem 1.1 in Section 1, immediately after defining ℓ and T and recalling the known rationality of Σ_{u∈W} x^{ℓ(u)}. The paper does not broaden the question, add auxiliary hypotheses, or give an equivalent reformulation nearby, so the sharpest faithful rewrite is essentially the official formulation with the hidden quantifier and the role of x made explicit. The statement is a problem, not a conjecture or theorem, and the paper adds that no partial results seem to be known.
